transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?
I came in because the doctor doing my insurance physical said my weight was too low. I mean, I just see myself as lean—I’m on ladders and working long days painting, so that’s how I figured I looked.
Have you been intentionally limiting how much you eat or trying to avoid gaining weight, or does your weight just tend to stay low despite eating normally?
Yeah, I guess I do limit it. Most days it’s just coffee, maybe a protein bar between paint jobs, then a small dinner. A full meal during the day feels like it would slow me down.

When you cut back on meals like that, is it mainly because you're worried that eating more would make you gain weight or change how your body looks, or is it more about not wanting to feel sluggish on the job?
It’s not just the work thing. If I see the scale go up, even a little—like after a client dinner or eating bread—I get tense. Then I’ll cut back the next day so it doesn’t stick.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you feel like you look too heavy or that certain parts of your body are too big, even though your doctor says you're underweight?

Yeah. When I catch myself in a mirror, or in photos standing next to one of my murals, I kind of judge the whole day by whether my stomach and face look sharp enough. If they don’t, I feel like I look bigger than I should.
Have you ever had episodes where you eat a large amount of food and feel out of control, or used vomiting, laxatives, or diuretics to prevent weight gain?
I’m not sure what would count as a large amount, honestly. I mostly just try not to eat enough to get to that point.
How long has this pattern of limiting your food intake and reacting to weight changes been going on—weeks, months, or longer?
It’s been going on for a while—months, at least. Most days I just have coffee, maybe a protein bar between paint jobs, then a small dinner. A full meal feels like it’d slow me down.
